ambiguities.description: Customer vs. Client terminology: The Product Manager clarified that CRM uses 'Customer' while the billing system uses 'Client', and that billing has a stricter definition (only counting paying entities as clients). The question is whether the billing definition is a formal constraint on the Customer entity (i.e., 'only paid customers count') or whether it is a separate business rule applied at the billing layer. Should the ORM model enforce that every Customer has made a payment, or is Customer defined more broadly and billing applies its own filter?

source_references.excerpt: One more thing -- I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing? Good question. In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Identification of OrderStatus: The transcript lists OrderStatus values (pending, confirmed, shipped, delivered) but does not explicitly state how to identify a unique OrderStatus value. Is OrderStatus simply identified by its text label, or could there be separate status codes? For modeling purposes, I have assumed OrderStatus is a simple value type with the four enumerated values, but if OrderStatus is actually a separate entity type (e.g., Status with a StatusId identifier), the model would need adjustment.
